Text.Text: When you enter now, the liturgy does not pause. It includes you. The blade drank, the soul rose, and I have nothing left to confess that your own edge hasn't already heard. Go. Sing it your own way.
Your blade is ready for more than your hands are. Reach rank 50 in Heavy Vibroblade, then return. There are verses I won't ask an unfinished pupil to carry.

Six Soul Ascension adepts are reciting my verses in the Forge Caverns. The people they cut are no longer offerings anyone chose to make. Defeat the six and bring me their heat ledger. I need to know what my congregation has been doing in my absence.
Take the key to the Forge Caverns entrance in the Sith Fortress forgeworks. Carry your blade carefully. It needn't answer every voice you hear.

A heavy blade takes. Every strike takes: breath, blood, warmth. Most spill what the blade takes and call it victory. Soul Ascension is the discipline of receiving it instead. The edge drinks, and what it drinks rises through your arms and mends you while you fight. From whom, you should ask. From those who chose to stand against you. That is the whole ethics of it, and you will doubt it later, and you should come ask me again when you do.

Mine. My voice taught them the first verse, and my exile is that they learned only the thirst. They drink without offering. No measure, no confession, no rising. Just edges that take and men who hollow. A rite practiced greedily isn't a rite anymore; it's feeding. Someone has to close their mouths, and I am done pretending it won't be by the sword.

Every heat, every quench, every blade the congregation ever fed, written in my hand and in theirs. In my liturgy, the ledger was the confession. The blade drinks, the debt is written down, and so the soul remembers what it owes. They kept writing long after they stopped confessing. I want the debt back where it can be read aloud.
Six adepts in the Forge Caverns. Bring their heat ledger here to the wasteland interiors. I will read the account.
You return on the exhale of the verse, exactly where you left it. And your pack is heavier with confession. Give it to me.

Sixty heats they never confessed... yes. This is the debt, carried up into the light, and that is the first verse whether you felt it happen or not. The blade drank tonight, and you stand here taller, not hollower. Notice that. Remember it. There is more liturgy below.

Five specialists are using a Sith tempering matrix in the caverns. They have made feeding the edge the whole rite. Beat the five and bring the matrix to me. There was meant to be more to ascension than that.
Bring the matrix here. Listen to what they're saying before you decide which parts of my rite they kept.

Mine, once. I won't pretend otherwise. In my liturgy it was the cup. The steel cooled through it and learned to receive what its edge would one day drink. A cup pours both ways; that was the whole point of it. They have soldered it into a mouth that only swallows. Bring it home and I will teach it to pour again.

You've felt it by now. The strike lands, and something warm walks up your arm and closes a wound you'd stopped noticing. That is the giving-back: the blade drinks and tithes to its bearer. The congregation hoards the tithe and wonders why they starve. Drink and offer, and the soul rises. Drink and keep, and the soul just widens. There is a difference. Pray you never learn it from the inside.

Don't say 'their master' as though he arrived from somewhere else. He was my first witness. He heard every verse I ever wrote and ascended past all of them, and what he is now sits at the bottom of my confession like a stone. Ask me again when you are stronger. By then I will owe you the answer.
Five specialists in the caverns hold the tempering matrix. Recover it after they're defeated.
I can hear it from here, flattering your pack straps, promising your blade an appetite. You didn't listen. Good. Hand it over.

There, cup. Home... Forgive me. One greets old relics, or one becomes the kind of man who melts them. Five deacons weighed and found wanting, and you stand here neither hollowed nor drunk on it. The second verse suits you. The third is louder.

The warden holds the Forge Caverns. Challenge him and return his cracked anvil sigil when he's defeated. Ask others to stand beside you. He has spent years taking strength from the people who came to him alone.

Witnesses, then. Choose them the way you'd choose pallbearers: for strength, and because you trust them with something of yours. When the warden falls, one of you will want to kneel a moment. Let them. Then bring me the shard.

The altar. Every rite needs one stone that does not move, and ours was the anvil. The blade drinks, the debt is written, and the oath is hammered true against that face. When he cracked it, he wasn't vandalizing. He was declaring the altar empty, and nothing owed to anyone. The sigil is his proof. Take it from him and the declaration dies.

His edge can take strength from a fight. Company makes it harder for him to choose every exchange. You may face him alone. I ask you to bring help because I would like you alive to question the doctrine afterward.

He held the anvil while I spoke the consecration. Held it, you understand. Bare hands on hot iron, because he believed a rite should cost the flesh something. I loved that in him, and the thirst found it first. When you face him, he won't taunt you. He will thank you for coming. Do not let that slow your arm.
Call the warden at the Forge Caverns challenge marker. Defeat him and return his anvil sigil.
You walk like a pallbearer. So it is done, and done properly. Show me what came off his neck.

He would thank you. He would... Enough. The altar's shard comes home, the vessel is broken, and I notice you shared the verse with others and came back more, not less. That is the entire lesson of the third verse, and most never learn it. Rest. The inner choir will have felt this.

Four overseers still have the clearance token. They authorize the congregation's work and call every consequence an offering. Defeat the four in the caverns and recover it. I'll read their names without the verses around them.
Recover the token. They will recite my own verses at you. You needn't accept their use of them.

Authority, stamped. Clearance to stand the deep floor, to sign heats, to admit and cast out. Everything a canon does, minted into a coin, because they couldn't carry the weight of the words. My liturgy issued nothing you could pocket. Bring me their token and I will show the caverns what authority without offering actually weighs.

I said I would owe you this, and you're strong enough now to collect. He drank past the rim. Ascension has a height, and a wise blade stops there. He did not stop. What sits in that sanctum wears his face, his guard, and my finest verse, and it is not rising anymore. It is a soul standing at its full height with nowhere left to go, drinking so it never has to look down. You will end him. I am long past pretending I want anything else.

Warmth, first. You've felt that. Then wounds close that you never showed the blade. And at the height of it, the fight goes quiet, and you can hear what your own soul is doing, which almost no one living gets to hear. That is the ascension, and it is worth every verse. It is also, drunk without offering, exactly what broke every man you have killed down there. Hold both truths at once. That is the fourth verse entire.
Four overseers in the caverns still have the clearance token. Bring it here when their work ends.
Quiet, below. The particular quiet a choir leaves behind it. The token, then. Let me hold their whole false church in one palm.

Stamped authority, already cooling... You have unmade their canon, witness. I use the word deliberately. You are one now: mine, and the rite's. One verse remains, and I won't insult you by pretending either of us needs to rehearse it.

The master is in the Champion Forge. Call him at its challenge marker and defeat him. He knows the rite as I wrote it. You know what it has cost. Come back afterward; I owe you an answer as much as a lesson.

Then go, and take one final instruction with you. When his soul spills, and it will spill, it is far too full for anything else, do not drink from it. Not out of mercy. Out of hygiene. Let it go down into the stone, where the forge can hold it. Yours must rise on its own weight, or the whole rite was for nothing.
Yes. He still has to choose where to strike and where to turn his guard. Help can make those choices harder. Don't try to match his hunger; make use of the openings his hunger makes him overlook.

Kneel, I think. Not to anything below. Just the ordinary kneeling of a man whose confession has finally caught up with his life. I built the rite. I chose the witness. I fled when it turned, and I sharpened you to end it. When you tell me it is done, my liturgy is done, and I will find out what an exile prays like when he is only an old man again. I confess I'm curious.

You ask. He never did. Keep people beside you who can question what you're doing, and keep listening when they do. I taught him to see every objection as weakness. You've brought me enough evidence to know what that lesson cost.
The Champion Forge holds the master's challenge marker. Defeat him, then return to me here. We still have something to discuss.
...and the blade is lowered, and the cup is poured, and the soul... Say it. Say the verse is finished.

The congregation is ended. I won't hide that behind a verse. Take your pay. If you still want Soul Ascension, I will teach it to someone who has seen where my words failed. I hope you will keep asking me what they mean.
One more question, priest.
Teach me. I'll bring back your ledger.
What is Soul Ascension?
What did your congregation become?
Why does a rite need a ledger?
Your liturgy can wait for me a little longer.
The Soul Ascension Forge Heat Ledger. The six adepts are silent.
The verse can hold. Another question.
I'll weigh your deacons myself.
What was the matrix in your rite?
What does the blade give back?
And the one they call master? Confess him.
Not yet. Keep your cup a while.
The Soul Ascension Sith Tempering Matrix. It flattered. I didn't listen.
Before the descent, a question.
I'll gather my witnesses and break your vessel.
What was the anvil to the rite?
Why witnesses? Say it plainly.
You knew this warden. Tell me.
My witnesses aren't gathered yet.
The Soul Ascension Cracked Anvil Sigil. He thanked us at the end.
Sing me one more answer first.
Four voices. We'll quiet the choir.
What does their token claim?
You owe me an answer. What is the master now?
What rises, when a soul rises?
Let the choir sing one day longer.
One Soul Ascension Overseer's Clearance Token, off your inner choir.
Not yet. Confess a little more.
We'll finish your liturgy. All of us together.
Can he be beaten at all?
And when he's gone? What's left for you?
Will I become what he became?
A last verse deserves ready witnesses. Not yet.
It's finished. His soul went down into the stone.
